title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, a healthy diet plays a crucial role in ensuring the well-being of both mother and baby. Iron and folate are two essential nutrients for fetal development. In this article, we will introduce three recipes rich in iron and folate that can be cooked in under 30 minutes, suitable for pregnant women's tastes and needs.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are vital for fetal development. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of the nervous system and prevents birth defects. To enhance iron absorption, combine iron-rich foods with vitamin C-rich foods.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken Bowl with Steamed Broccoli and Lemon
* 100g grilled chicken
* 100g steamed broccoli
* 1/2 lemon
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Grill chicken in the oven at 200°C for 20 minutes. Steam broccoli in boiling water for 5 minutes. Mix all ingredients with olive oil, salt, and pepper. This simple recipe provides approximately 10mg of iron and 100mcg of folate.

## Recipe 2: Beef Stir-Fry Bowl with Spinach and Bell Peppers
* 100g beef stir-fry
* 100g spinach
* 1/2 bell pepper
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Stir-fry beef in a pan with olive oil at medium heat for 10 minutes. Steam spinach in boiling water for 5 minutes. Mix all ingredients with bell pepper, salt, and pepper. This recipe provides approximately 15mg of iron and 150mcg of folate.

## Recipe 3: Baked Salmon Bowl with Mixed Greens and Lemon
* 100g baked salmon
* 100g mixed greens
* 1/2 lemon
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Bake salmon in the oven at 200°C for 20 minutes. Steam mixed greens in boiling water for 5 minutes. Mix all ingredients with olive oil, salt, and pepper. This recipe provides approximately 10mg of iron and 100mcg of folate.

## Food Safety Notes
When pregnant, avoid eating raw or undercooked foods, especially meat, eggs, and seafood. Cook foods at high temperatures to ensure safety.

## Conclusion
These three recipes provide a rich source of iron and folate, supporting fetal development. For a healthy diet, consult our [meal planner](/planner) and [prenatal nutrition category](/blog/prenatal-nutrition) on our website.

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about your diet during pregnancy, consult your doctor or a registered dietitian.
